lectures.title: What is TypeScript and Why would you use it?

cues.en: So what exactly is Typescript, that's important to understand right
because without knowing that, it will be hard to learn it and to use it.
Now it's important to understand and I really want to stress this, that Typescript is not a brand new
language with a totally different syntax,
no, it builds up on Javascript,
it is a so-called superset to Javascript which in the end means it is Javascript but it adds more
features, more syntax features you can use.
Now it is worth noting, as I mentioned, that Typescript does not run in browsers, browsers don't know how
to execute Typescript, they know how to execute Javascript.
So whilst you will learn how to write Typescript in this module here, it's not a language you can use
like this in browsers, instead and that's of course also something you learn in this module, we need
an extra tool which compiles Typescript code to Javascript code, so which converts the code to Javascript
so that we have the Javascript code we learned about but during development when we write Typescript code, we have
a better experience because of all these extra features.
Now speaking of that, which features does Typescript add?
Well most importantly the thing that gives Typescript its name, it adds types
and with that, I mean data types.
Now of course in Javascript, we also know types, you learned about the core types Javascript has - strings,
numbers, boolean, objects and so on.
Now it is important to understand that Javascript is a dynamic, weakly typed language which means that
types are evaluated during runtime,
so when your script executes but they're not something you define when you write your code, of course
you might know that here you're working with a string and in another place you're working with a number
but you're not putting that into your code
and let me give you an example where this might matter. Consider this simple add function which adds
two numbers, presumably at least
but now let's say you're calling this function with two strings which you're passing in, please notice
the quotes around the numbers.
Now of course you might wonder why you would do that
but consider that this is coming from an input field in your DOM, in your web page,
what you get from there will always be a string
so even if the user enters a number there, it's technically will be a string.
Now if you add these two strings here, you will actually find a bug in your application.
It will not crash or show an error
but what you will get is basically the concatenated strings and I can quickly show this to you here in
the normal Javascript console in a browser,
if I add five plus three, we get 53 as a string because it simply concatenates those instead of adding
them.
Now that's probably undesired and in Typescript,
you can avoid this because in Typescript, you can add types and this is now a syntax feature which
is added by Typescript, which does not exist in Javascript. Notice the colons after a and b in the parameter
list of the function
and after the colon you see the word number.
This is Typescript syntax which in the end tells Typescript that both a and b in this case here
should be of type number,
so we must only call this function with two numbers being fed in, not with two strings.
So here in Typescript, when we compile this to Javascript, I mentioned that it needs to be compiled, we
will get a compile time error, giving us as a developer a chance of fixing this before we even test it
in the browser so we can catch errors or bugs like this way earlier
and that's the huge thing about Typescript or one of the huge things. Now besides adding types, Typescript
also adds some other nice features which don't exist like this in Javascript, of course these features
since Typescript doesn't run in browsers are always compiled down to Javascript workarounds to make the
same feature work there as well but in Typescript, it's often easier to implement certain things thanks to
these extra features
and in addition, Typescript also compilers next generation Javascript code to old generation Javascript
code you could say.
So the thing Babel does, the tool we learned about in the browser support module, Typescript actually
has this built in. Typescript also allows you to write modern Javascript Typescript code in the Typescript
files and as a result, get Javascript files which will run in older browsers as well.
So Typescript sounds pretty interesting to me,
let's take a closer look at it,
let's see how we install that compiler and let's write some Typescript code.
